src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: FulfilmentService is constructed with `private readonly products: ProductRepository, private readonly orders: OrderRepository` and does all persistence through these ports.
src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: TRANSITION_TARGET is the only place that maps Transition to OrderState, and transition() hands the state change to the domain function advance().
src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: the not-found checks live once, in getProduct/getOrder, and placeOrder, transition and cancelOrder reuse them.
src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: stock is changed only through the domain functions reserveStock/releaseStock, with rollback in placeOrder and release in cancelOrder.
src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: cancelOrder uses this.products.get rather than getProduct, which appears deliberate so a missing product is skipped instead of throwing.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit covers one concern, order fulfilment, and it is the application layer's use cases plus the ports they need. ports.ts declares the ProductRepository and OrderRepository interfaces. FulfilmentService receives both through constructor injection and talks to persistence only through those ports, so nothing goes around the module's own abstractions. State changes are handed to the domain functions advance, cancel, reserveStock and releaseStock instead of being reimplemented here. Each rule appears once within the unit: TRANSITION_TARGET is the single map from Transition names to OrderState, the not-found checks live in getProduct and getOrder and are reused, and input validation for placing orders and adding products appears only once. One small inconsistency: cancelOrder calls this.products.get instead of getProduct. That looks deliberate, since stock release should simply skip a missing product rather than throw, so it doesn't count as a bypass. addProduct checks that stock is a non-negative integer and builds the Product literal itself. The domain module isn't included here, so I can't confirm whether this repeats a check in the domain. Nothing visible fails the rubric.
